svg.title: Trusting the installer on a fresh machine: Without sudo rights, the task installer puts task in the developer's own folder
svg.text: Trusting the installer on a fresh machine
Scenario: Without sudo rights, the task installer puts task in the developer's own folder

g.text: Given a fresh machine where the developer has no sudo rights and task is
A brand-new Ubuntu machine where the developer has no sudo rights, with the toolbox's task
installer in .config/task. One typed line: sudo asks for a password, /usr/local/bin belongs
to root, and task is not installed.
Then the task installer puts task in ~/.local/bin, says that folder must be on the PATH, and
The developer runs the task installer. It cannot write to /usr/local/bin and has no sudo, so it says it installs into
/home/bootstrap/.local/bin instead, the developer's own folder. The lines after it come from task's official install
The installer then says where task is and that this folder must be on the PATH. The run ends with exit code 0, and the
shell finds task in /home/bootstrap/.local/bin. Versions show as <version>, the download progress and the temporary
folder as placeholders: they change with each run or update.

text.tspan: sh .config/task/install.sh; echo "exit code: $?"; command -v task; task --version
